bibl.title: A systemic approach to the psychology of racial bias within individuals and society

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: The two-way relation between racial biases held by individuals and the societal systems those individuals live in, in the USA.
span.quote: We consider the effects of five systemic factors on racial biases in the USA: power and privilege disparities, cultural narratives and values, segregated communities, shared stereotypes and nonverbal messages.

span.label: If racial bias is produced by systems rather than only held by people, what does psychology miss by measuring it one person at a time?
span.quote: However, this approach largely ignores the systemic nature of racial biases and the ways in which racial biases are shaped by the broader cultural systems in which people live 12 – 14 .

span.label: A nested-levels framework in which five systemic factors shape individual bias and individual bias feeds back to reproduce those systems.
span.quote: We argue that systemic factors operating across levels — from the interpersonal to the cultural — contribute to the production and reinforcement of racial biases in children and adults.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: We argue that systemic factors operating across levels — from the interpersonal to the cultural — contribute to the production and reinforcement of racial biases in children and adults.

span.label: racial bias
span.quote: Racial bias refers to favouring or providing preferential treatment to members of one racial group over another.

span.label: review
span.quote: In this Review, we examine the bidirectional relation between individual-level racial biases and broader societal systems through a systemic lens.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Children raised in an unequal society, given no systemic explanation for that inequality, internalize the existing distribution of power and privilege as legitimate
span.quote: Children who are socialized in an unequal society, without systemic explanations for why power and privilege have been concentrated among certain people, often internalize that system 34 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Internalized expectations of inequality drive behaviour that maintains the system, so individual attitudes reproduce the very inequality that generated them (a self-reinforcing loop)
span.quote: These beliefs and expectations then motivate the individuals that make up the system to behave in ways that maintain the system of inequality, such that individuals’ attitudes reinforce the system of inequality that produced them.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Nonverbal bias propagates as an expanding transmission system: seeing biased signals creates biased attitudes, which are then expressed as biased signals that others in the social network observe and adopt
span.quote: Thus, nonverbal biases can be thought of as an expanding system of transmission wherein exposure to nonverbal biases contributes to the development of racially biased attitudes; those attitudes then manifest as biased nonverbal signals, which others within the social network will then see, leading them to develop biases, and so on 233 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Devaluing cultural products lets people transmit racial bias while believing they are only judging the product, hiding the bias from the person holding it
span.quote: This contribution to individual-level racial bias is particularly insidious because it creates conditions under which people can obliviously perpetuate racial biases, believing their bias to be against the cultural products they perceive as inferior rather than the people associated with the products.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: system justification: growing up inside an unequal arrangement without an explanation for it leads children and adults to conclude the arrangement is right
span.quote: Both children and adults tend to conclude that the way things are structured in society is the way they should be 35 – 42 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: structural exposure predicts individual bias - the composition of a university, a neighbourhood's poverty rate, a community's economic mobility all track measured implicit bias
span.quote: Attending a university with few faculty members of colour, living in an area that has high poverty rates among Black residents and living in a community with low economic mobility all predict heightened implicit bias against Black people among non-Black American residents 7 , 46 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: backlash: information that inequality is decreasing can raise bias rather than lower it
span.quote: White residents of the USA who were exposed to information about the increasing racial diversity of the USA subsequently exhibited increased bias favouring white people relative to those who were not exposed to this information 47 – 50 .

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the return path: aggregate individual bias in a county tracks institutional outcomes such as school discipline, so attitudes reconstitute the systems that produced them
span.quote: In American counties where the individual-level bias against Black people is stronger, there are larger racial disparities in school disciplinary actions, with Black students being subjected to more suspensions, expulsions, and referrals to law enforcement than white students 58 .

span.label: Scope is restricted to the USA, chosen for the authors' cultural knowledge and the location of most existing research.
span.quote: We focus on the USA because it is the context that we have the cultural knowledge to discuss and where most research on racial bias development has been conducted.

span.label: The five systemic factors reviewed are a selection, not an exhaustive set.
span.quote: Although they are certainly not the only systemic factors that influence racial biases, we focus on these five because we believe them to be particularly relevant to the development of racial biases in the contemporary USA.

span.label: For part of the reviewed evidence the direction of influence between individual bias and system is not established, only association.
span.quote: In some cases, there is clear evidence of the causal chain from system to individual and from individual to system, whereas in others, there might be evidence of an association, but the direction of influence is unclear.

span.label: The empirical base linking systemic influences to individual-level bias is described as still thin.
span.quote: Although there is a growing body of literature tying systemic influences to individual-level biases, the literature in this area is still relatively sparse.

span.label: Restricted to the USA by the authors' own statement, and the paper says the systemic factors may not transfer.
span.quote: Given this history of racism in the USA, the systemic factors that perpetuate racial biases into the present might be somewhat distinct from other contexts.

span.label: The causal direction is not established throughout - in places only an association is available.
span.quote: In some cases, there is clear evidence of the causal chain from system to individual and from individual to system, whereas in others, there might be evidence of an association, but the direction of influence is unclear.

span.label: The five factors are chosen, not exhaustive, and the authors say so.
span.quote: Although they are certainly not the only systemic factors that influence racial biases, we focus on these five because we believe them to be particularly relevant to the development of racial biases in the contemporary USA.

span.label: Mutual reinforcement is treated as two separable directions for expositional clarity, which is an analytic simplification the paper flags.
span.quote: In many cases, individual-level biases and broader societal systems might be mutually reinforcing, but for clarity we take the approach of assessing each direction of influence separately.

span.label: the nested-levels model of influence, imported to relate individual racial bias to the systems around it
span.quote: Models of nested levels of influence in the study of race relations 17 , human development 18 and culture 19 , 20 can be used to consider the relation between racial bias and broader systemic factors (Fig. 1 ).

span.label: racial bias
span.quote: Racial bias refers to favouring or providing preferential treatment to members of one racial group over another.

span.label: systemic factors
span.quote: We argue that systemic factors operating across levels — from the interpersonal to the cultural — contribute to the production and reinforcement of racial biases in children and adults.

span.label: individual-level
span.quote: Historically, the field of psychology has focused on racial biases at an individual level, considering the effects of various stimuli on individual racial attitudes and biases.

span.label: nested levels of influence
span.quote: Models of nested levels of influence in the study of race relations 17 , human development 18 and culture 19 , 20 can be used to consider the relation between racial bias and broader systemic factors (Fig. 1 ).

span.label: temporal influences
span.quote: At the outermost level are temporal influences, which capture how past interpersonal, institutional or community, and societal influences continue to influence members of society throughout their lives.

span.label: power and privilege
span.quote: We consider the effects of five systemic factors on racial biases in the USA: power and privilege disparities, cultural narratives and values, segregated communities, shared stereotypes and nonverbal messages.

span.label: cultural narratives
span.quote: In educational curricula in the USA, national history tends to be taught through a white-affirming lens, such that the attitudes, values and perspectives of white people are implicitly or explicitly justified by the historical narrative 60 , 61 .

span.label: implicit bias
span.quote: Attending a university with few faculty members of colour, living in an area that has high poverty rates among Black residents and living in a community with low economic mobility all predict heightened implicit bias against Black people among non-Black American residents 7 , 46 .

span.label: cultural context
span.quote: Communities are situated within a broader cultural context that shapes the norms, values, and beliefs that structure society.

span.label: bias - a property of a PERSON: an attitude favouring one group, measured on individuals in response to stimuli
span.quote: Historically, the field of psychology has focused on racial biases at an individual level, considering the effects of various stimuli on individual racial attitudes and biases.

span.label: bias - a property of a SYSTEM: patterns built into institutions and culture, which produce individual attitudes rather than summing them
span.quote: However, this approach largely ignores the systemic nature of racial biases and the ways in which racial biases are shaped by the broader cultural systems in which people live 12 – 14 .

span.label: level - a nested shell of context around the person: interpersonal, community, cultural, temporal
span.quote: At the innermost level are the most proximal influences on individual-level racial bias — personal and interpersonal experiences, such as socialization from caregivers and interracial friendships.

span.label: builds-on → Caste: The Origins Of Our Discontents
span.quote: Some of these similarities are highlighted in the book Caste: The Origins Of Our Discontents 29 — which draws parallels between the systems of oppression of Black people in the USA, Jewish people in Nazi Germany and Dalit people in India.

span.label: builds-on → prior arguments (ref. 11) that individuals and systems mutually reinforce one another in organizations and the workplace
span.quote: Similar arguments about individuals and systems mutually reinforcing one another have been made in the context of organizations and the workplace 11 .

span.label: contradicts → the individual-level tradition in the psychology of racial bias
span.quote: Historically, the field of psychology has focused on racial biases at an individual level, considering the effects of various stimuli on individual racial attitudes and biases.

span.label: extends → nested-levels models from race relations, human development and culture research
span.quote: Models of nested levels of influence in the study of race relations 17 , human development 18 and culture 19 , 20 can be used to consider the relation between racial bias and broader systemic factors (Fig. 1 ).

span.label: systemic factors —causes→ racial bias
span.quote: We argue that systemic factors operating across levels — from the interpersonal to the cultural — contribute to the production and reinforcement of racial biases in children and adults.

span.label: racial bias —causes→ systemic factors
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the reverse of the edge above, and asserted in the same sentence. The paper's claim is that the two directions form a loop; the eight edge types cannot say 'bidirectional', so it is two edges. See HANDOFF/tagging_open_questions.md Q-12.
span.quote: Each level of influence influences the innermost level of individual attitudes, and conversely, individual-level attitudes also influence systems 21 .

span.label: individual-level —contrasted-with→ systemic factors
span.quote: However, this approach largely ignores the systemic nature of racial biases and the ways in which racial biases are shaped by the broader cultural systems in which people live 12 – 14 .

span.label: power and privilege —part-of→ systemic factors
span.quote: We consider the effects of five systemic factors on racial biases in the USA: power and privilege disparities, cultural narratives and values, segregated communities, shared stereotypes and nonverbal messages.

span.label: cultural narratives —part-of→ systemic factors
span.quote: We consider the effects of five systemic factors on racial biases in the USA: power and privilege disparities, cultural narratives and values, segregated communities, shared stereotypes and nonverbal messages.

span.label: temporal influences —part-of→ nested levels of influence
span.quote: At the outermost level are temporal influences, which capture how past interpersonal, institutional or community, and societal influences continue to influence members of society throughout their lives.

span.label: cultural context —part-of→ nested levels of influence
span.quote: Communities are situated within a broader cultural context that shapes the norms, values, and beliefs that structure society.

span.label: The review argues that five specific systemic factors — power and privilege disparities, cultural narratives and values, segregated communities, shared stereotypes and nonverbal messages — produce and reinforce individual-level racial bias in the USA.
span.quote: We consider the effects of five systemic factors on racial biases in the USA: power and privilege disparities, cultural narratives and values, segregated communities, shared stereotypes and nonverbal messages.

span.label: The relation runs in both directions: each of the five systemic factors shapes individual-level bias, and individual-level bias in turn shapes systems and inequalities at every nested level.
span.quote: We provided evidence that each of these five systemic factors shapes individual-level racial biases, and that individual-level racial biases shape systems and inequalities at each of the nested levels.

span.label: Telling white Americans that the country is becoming more racially diverse increases, rather than decreases, their bias in favour of white people.
span.quote: White residents of the USA who were exposed to information about the increasing racial diversity of the USA subsequently exhibited increased bias favouring white people relative to those who were not exposed to this information 47 – 50 .

span.label: Living in a state with a larger Black population raises racial bias only for white residents who lack close contact with Black people, so proximity without relationship is what increases bias.
span.quote: A follow-up study examined how this pattern relates to intergroup contact, finding that living in a state with more Black residents was only associated with increased racial bias among white residents who had limited close contact with Black people 144 .

span.label: Colourblind ideology functions to keep policies that are formally race-neutral racially biased in their effects.
span.quote: Overall, racially colourblind ideology has allowed systemic policies that are ostensibly race-neutral to remain racially biased in effect.

span.label: Because the cultural products of people of colour (art, dress, speech) are devalued at a societal level, individuals develop bias against the people who use and produce those products.
span.quote: In summary, the cultural products of people of colour are devalued and stigmatized at a societal level, which results in individual-level biases against those who use and produce these cultural products.

span.label: Individual bias devalues and negatively stereotypes physical spaces occupied by people of colour, which makes those spaces less desirable to white people and so reinforces residential segregation.
span.quote: Overall, individual-level racial biases can contribute to the devaluation and negative stereotyping of physical spaces occupied by people of colour, which make those spaces less desirable to white people—reinforcing racial segregation.

span.label: The causal effect of exposure to cultural products on racial attitudes has never been tested experimentally, which the authors identify as an open gap.
span.quote: For instance, it has yet to be experimentally tested how exposure to cultural products influences racial attitudes.

span.label: Markers of structural inequality in a person's surroundings predict their measured implicit bias.
span.quote: Attending a university with few faculty members of colour, living in an area that has high poverty rates among Black residents and living in a community with low economic mobility all predict heightened implicit bias against Black people among non-Black American residents 7 , 46 .

span.label: Being told the country is becoming more diverse increased pro-white bias rather than reducing it.
span.quote: White residents of the USA who were exposed to information about the increasing racial diversity of the USA subsequently exhibited increased bias favouring white people relative to those who were not exposed to this information 47 – 50 .

span.label: Aggregate individual bias tracks institutional outcomes: county-level bias predicts racial disparities in school suspensions, expulsions and police referrals.
span.quote: In American counties where the individual-level bias against Black people is stronger, there are larger racial disparities in school disciplinary actions, with Black students being subjected to more suspensions, expulsions, and referrals to law enforcement than white students 58 .

span.label: Individual bias also tracks voting and policy support, giving a route from attitudes back to national institutions.
span.quote: Greater individual-level anti-Black bias was associated with a lower likelihood of voting for Barack Obama in the 2008 American presidential election and reduced support for his healthcare reform proposal 52 , 53 .

span.label: The individual-level framing has produced an intervention industry the authors judge unlikely to address the causes.
span.quote: Although potentially useful for changing individual attitudes and/or biases, these interventions seem unlikely to adequately address the underlying causes of bias, which stem from the systems and structures that create and reinforce racial inequality.

span.label: racial bias
span.quote: Racial bias refers to favouring or providing preferential treatment to members of one racial group over another.

span.label: intergroup contact
span.quote: Ongoing segregation also limits intergroup contact 138 — contact between people belonging to different racial or ethnic groups — one of the most reliable and best studied predictors of reduced individual-level bias 139 .

span.label: racial socialization
span.quote: One potential lever with which to reduce the spread of individual racial biases is for white parents to teach their children directly about the importance of race and racism (as parents of colour do), a process called racial socialization.

span.label: redlining
span.quote: For instance, ‘redlining’ was a mid-twentieth-century policy in which neighbourhoods were graded (from ‘desirable’ to ‘hazardous’) according to their supposed risk of decreasing in value.

span.label: racially colourblind ideology
span.quote: Racially colourblind ideology (the idea of disregarding the issue of race) is another cultural philosophy that can contribute to the perpetuation of individual-level racial biases.

span.label: eminent domain
span.quote: Eminent domain — a legal power that forces private citizens to sell land to the government for public projects —is more likely to be used in communities of colour 154 , 155 and has myriad negative consequences, including loss of wealth and disruption of community ties and stability 156 , 157 .

span.label: manifest destiny
span.quote: As an example, ‘manifest destiny’ (the worldview that white people were destined to expand their territory to the west coast of North America) is often presented uncritically as a justification for atrocities that white people committed against the original Native American and Mexican inhabitants of the continent 60 , 71 .

span.label: racial bias
span.quote: Racial bias refers to favouring or providing preferential treatment to members of one racial group over another.

span.label: the nested levels of influence
span.quote: At the innermost level are the most proximal influences on individual-level racial bias — personal and interpersonal experiences, such as socialization from caregivers and interracial friendships.

span.label: temporal influences, the outermost level
span.quote: At the outermost level are temporal influences, which capture how past interpersonal, institutional or community, and societal influences continue to influence members of society throughout their lives.

span.label: approximately 40% — share of US residents in 2020 polling who thought that paying less attention to race would improve racial inequality
span.quote: Polling data from 2020 indicated that approximately 40% of American residents believed that paying less attention to race would improve racial inequalities in society 116 .

span.label: roughly five times — Black-to-white ratio of US incarceration rates as of 2021
span.quote: As of 2021, Black Americans were incarcerated at roughly five times the rate of white Americans 268 , 269 .

span.label: 75% — share of neighbours who are white for the average white American, as an index of residential segregation
span.quote: For instance, the average white American lives in a neighbourhood whose residents are 75% white 133 .

span.label: 40% — proportion of preschool children exposed to biased nonverbal signals who then copied those signals themselves
span.quote: Furthermore, 40% of preschool children who were exposed to biased nonverbal signals in a study mimicked the biased nonverbal signals they observed 232 .

span.label: 67% ... less than 8% — share of South African top management positions held by white people in 2017, versus their share of the population
span.quote: Power and privilege disparities in South Africa are stark; in 2017 white people held 67% of the top management positions but accounted for less than 8% of the country’s population 272 .

span.label: 100 times higher — the War on Drugs sentencing ratio between substances used disproportionately by Black versus white Americans
span.quote: One of its most notorious policies set a penalty 100 times higher for possession of substances that were disproportionately used by Black American residents than for substances disproportionately used by white American residents 210 .

span.label: 57% ... 30% — how often observers attributed their attitude towards a target to the target's own behaviour rather than to the biased treatment the target received
span.quote: Even when the targets of (positively or negatively) biased nonverbal signals displayed identical behaviours, observers were more likely to report that the targets’ behaviour (57%), rather than how the target was treated (30%), influenced their attitudes towards the target 223 , 227 .

span.label: five systemic factors — the factors the review covers: power and privilege, cultural narratives and values, segregated communities, shared stereotypes, nonverbal messages
span.quote: We consider the effects of five systemic factors on racial biases in the USA: power and privilege disparities, cultural narratives and values, segregated communities, shared stereotypes and nonverbal messages.

span.label: systemic factors - structural inequality, cultural narratives, segregation, stereotypes, nonverbal signals
span.term: systemic factors - structural inequality, cultural narratives, segregation, stereotypes, nonverbal signals
span.quote: We argue that systemic factors operating across levels — from the interpersonal to the cultural — contribute to the production and reinforcement of racial biases in children and adults.
